rv.q: Imaginative political drama lays bare the barriers faced by the international aid system
The production feels longer than its 90-minute duration.
A FINE IDEA indeed, but not fully a fine play… yet.
A Fine Idea is indeed a fine idea for a play, but this stuff is hard to pull off successfully.
If you’d like to go back to secondary school, then A Fine Idea is the play for you.
I only hope stories like ‘A Fine Idea’ continue to be told.
Despite the talented cast, the relationships often felt forced as they served as a vehicle for the polemic.
The play delivers the issues at hand in a palatable way.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this political drama about international development, praising its thought-provoking subject matter but faulting its didactic, statistics-heavy approach that tells rather than shows.
